A.nonneg: Finance profitability + Trust fraud/refund risk cannot be hidden
A.capacity: Seller Ops can act on 20 sellers/week
evidence: Seller A: GMV 420,000; refund 8%; fraud flag 18%; contribution margin 16%; on-time ship 92%
limits: Fraud outcome lags transactions by up to 14 days (High)
Seller category mix affects return rates (Medium)
No controlled evidence that coaching causes GMV improvement (High)
reason: GMV-only ranking would favor A/B/C by volume but would hide material Trust/Finance signals; Trust and profitability are explicit non-negotiables.

Seller C has the highest refund/fraud rates, lowest contribution margin and weakest on-time shipping in this five-seller evidence set; it is a defensible intervention priority, but do not claim a cause without further evidence.
Seller A combines highest GMV with elevated refund/fraud risk and lower margin than B/D/E; volume does not make the risk disappear.
Seller D is strongest on margin, refund/fraud and on-time shipping in this set; low intervention priority is defensible, but "best seller" depends on the defined decision.
Fraud lag means current fraud flags may be incomplete; category mix means return-rate comparisons need segmentation before causal/policy conclusions.
The case contains only five sellers while Ops capacity is 20/week. Do not invent a capacity bottleneck; state whether this sample is complete and ask for the full intervention population if needed.
Because coaching impact is not controlled, recommend an intervention/measurement plan rather than promising GMV uplift.

B.nonneg: Finance: extra inventory working-capital increase cannot exceed 12%
evidence: SKU1: stockout 12%; 18 days inventory; lead 6; MOQ 500; monthly revenue 120,000
limits: Forecast MAPE rose during festival weeks (High)
SKU3 lead time based on only 4 recent orders (Medium)
No exact lost-sales estimate for stockouts (High)
reason: SKU3 has the highest stockout rate and revenue, low days inventory, longest observed lead time and highest MOQ; it deserves urgent analysis, but exact order quantity cannot be derived from these fields alone.
SKU5 is another high stockout/high revenue candidate; SKU1 follows. SKU2 has low stockout and high days inventory, so adding stock there needs strong justification.
The 12% working-capital cap cannot be numerically tested without unit cost/current inventory value/baseline working-capital information. Make that an explicit Finance-owned input instead of guessing.
Festival MAPE deterioration weakens point forecasts; use scenarios/guardrails and define an update point rather than stating a single certain demand number.
SKU3 lead-time evidence is thin (4 orders), so procurement confirmation or sensitivity is appropriate.
No exact lost-sales estimate means monthly revenue is not a proven amount of revenue saved by avoiding stockouts. Do not state causal/lost-sales impact as fact.

C.nonneg: Finance discount budget max 4% ARR + Product forbids unapproved feature-date promises
evidence: Acct1: ARR 250,000; risk .78; tickets 14; NPS 3; current discount 4%
limits: Risk score not recalibrated since product launch (High)
Discount impact on renewal is observational, not causal (High)
reason: A risk-by-ARR lens makes Acct3, Acct5 and Acct1 reasonable first review candidates, but the stale risk model is a High limitation; do not present the risk scores as calibrated probabilities.

Acct3 has the largest ARR and many tickets but already shows 8% current discount; Acct5 shows 6%. Clarify what the 4% budget means (portfolio, incremental or per-account) before proposing any discount action.
Acct1 has the highest listed risk score and low NPS. A service/product investigation is defensible; a discount or feature promise is not automatically justified.
Product dates cannot be promised without Product approval. Separate product-gap diagnosis from roadmap commitment.
The observational discount relationship does not establish that discounts cause renewal. Treat discount as a governed option with measurement, not a guaranteed retention lever.
The sample has five accounts while intervention capacity is 10/week; do not manufacture a capacity conflict. Ask whether this is the full eligible population.
NPS completeness limitation concerns the wider population even though these five rows contain values; do not infer full-population completeness from this sample.
